dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL student project; uses inline comments with *>, EVALUATE/END-EVALUATE, PERFORM WITH TEST AFTER, ACCEPT FROM DATE YYYYMMDD, and free-form paragraph names typical of GnuCOBOL usage. French-language identifiers and menus suggest a French academic environment.
evidence: ORGANIZATION INDEXED with ALTERNATE RECORD KEY
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS

purpose.domain_detail: Tribunal/court management system (GésTrib = Gestion Tribunal): manages jurors, hearings (séances), convocations, courtrooms (salles), and legal cases (affaires) for a French court.
purpose.summary: A menu-driven batch COBOL application for managing a French tribunal. It handles CRUD operations for jurors, convocations, hearings, courtrooms, and legal cases, with business rules such as minimum 7-day notice for hearings and minimum juror age of 21. It also provides utility functions like finding non-compliant hearings.

notable_features: Multiple indexed files with alternate record keys and duplicates
Sequential temp files for update-in-place pattern
ACCEPT FROM DATE YYYYMMDD for current date
PERFORM WITH TEST AFTER loops (do-while style)
No GOTO usage despite complex flow (154 PERFORMs)
Age validation logic for juror eligibility
START with KEY EQUALS for alternate key navigation
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full program is 1823 lines. Program name 'ProjetGesTrib' strongly suggests a student project (Projet = Project in French). Logic appears reasonably complete for a student exercise but has some inconsistencies (e.g., OPEN OUTPUT FSeances in ConsulterProchainesSeances instead of OPEN INPUT). No COPY statements or subprogram CALLs used.
